Myrtle Beach Vacation Home: Second Home or Investment Property Loan?

Buying a beach place you'll use and rent out sometimes? Here's how lenders decide, and what Horry County taxes will look like.

Paul Hankins
Founder & Broker · NMLS #281393

Buying a vacation home in Myrtle Beach, North Myrtle Beach or Surfside Beach? Your loan comes down to how you'll use it. It's a second home if you'll stay there part of the year and keep control of it, even if you rent it out some weeks. It's an investment property if you won't stay there, a rental company controls the bookings, or you need the rent to qualify for the loan.

Which one is your beach house?

Can I rent out my second home?

Yes. You can rent out a second home and still keep a second home loan. Two things have to stay true. You stay there yourself for part of the year. And the rent isn't used to qualify you for the loan.

What you can't do is hand control to someone else. Listing the house yourself is fine, and so is hiring a manager, as long as you decide when the house is booked. Signing up for a rental program that decides when you're allowed to stay is not. That turns it into an investment property.

Why the label matters

The same house can get two very different loans:

  • Down payment. With a Fannie Mae loan, an investment property needs a bigger down payment than a second home when you buy.
  • Cost. Fannie Mae adds a charge to every investment property loan, and to some second home loans. It shows up in the rate or as a fee at closing.
  • Rent. On an investment property, the rent can help you qualify. A DSCR loan can even qualify you on the rent.

Your exact down payment depends on your credit, the price and the loan, so a loan officer gives you that number when you pre-qualify.

Second home mortgage requirements

For a second home loan sold to Fannie Mae, the home must:

  • be lived in by you for some part of the year (there's no set number of days);
  • be a single house or condo, not a duplex or larger;
  • be livable all year;
  • be under your control, with no rental program or manager deciding who stays there;
  • not be a timeshare.

Buying a condo? The building has its own rules too. See Myrtle Beach condo financing.

Property taxes on a Myrtle Beach second home

Out-of-state buyers should know this one. South Carolina gives your main home two big breaks. It's assessed at 4% of its value instead of 6%, and it's exempt from school operating taxes. A second home or rental gets neither.

The result in Horry County: a second home or rental's tax bill runs about 3.3 times what an owner who lives there pays on the same house, and about 4.3 times inside the City of Myrtle Beach. Plan for that in your budget. Your loan officer will use the second home tax figure when working out what you can afford.

Renting it out: local rules and taxes

  • Lodging taxes. A short-term rental inside the City of Myrtle Beach collects about 13% in lodging taxes on each stay. South Carolina counts any stay under 90 days in a row as short-term.
  • North Myrtle Beach. The city requires a business license to rent short-term.
  • Condos. If the building has a front desk or a required rental program, it can affect both your loan type and whether the building qualifies. See Myrtle Beach condo financing.

Be honest about how you'll use it

On your loan application, you say how you'll use the home. Calling a rental a second home to get better terms is a false statement on a loan application, and that's a federal crime. Plans can change later in life. If you want to turn your second home into a full-time rental down the road, talk to your loan officer first.

Near the water? Check the flood zone too: flood insurance in Myrtle Beach. Already own a home with equity? You can also buy a second home with a cash-out refinance.

Second home loan questions

Can I rent out my Myrtle Beach second home?

Yes, as long as you stay there part of the year, keep control of the bookings, and don't use the rent to qualify for the loan. Short-term stays in the City of Myrtle Beach collect about 13% in lodging taxes.

How many days do you have to live in a second home?

Fannie Mae's second home rule doesn't set a number of days. You must live there for some part of the year, and the home must be livable year-round.

Can I use rental income to qualify for a second home?

No. If you need the rent to qualify, the loan is an investment property loan. A DSCR loan, which qualifies you on the rent, is one option.

Are property taxes higher on a second home in Myrtle Beach?

Yes. A second home or rental in Horry County pays about 3.3 times what an owner-occupant pays on the same house, and about 4.3 times inside the City of Myrtle Beach. Your main home gets a 4% assessment and a school tax exemption that a second home doesn't.
